Consider the following statements
1.
Assertion (A): Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued a new gold coin which was called Dinar by Ibn Battuta.
2.
Reason (R): Muhammad bin Tughlaq wanted to issue token currency in gold coins to promote trade with West Asian and North African countries.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced a new gold coin known as the Dinar (called Dinar by Ibn Battuta). He also issued a silver coin called the Adli and undertook important currency reforms during his reign. Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced a token currency around 1330 CE to tackle the shortage of silver in the royal treasury. Drawing inspiration from the currency system used in China under Kublai Khan, he issued copper coins (Jitals) and set their value at the same level as silver tankas. However, since the concept of token currency was unfamiliar in India and there was no effective control over minting, counterfeit coins were produced on a large scale. The widespread forgery disrupted the economy and undermined public confidence in the currency. Consequently, the Sultan withdrew the scheme and agreed to exchange the copper coins for silver coins.

s: Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq had transferred his capital from Delhi to –
x: Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq had shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devgiri). It was one of the most significant experiments of Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq. Various factors have been identified for this experiment. According to Barani, Devgiri probably was at the center of his empire. According to Ibn Battuta, the people of Delhi used to write undeferential letters to Sultan. To punish them he decided to make Devgiri his capital. Muhammad Tughluq was also the first Sultan of Delhi who tried to establish the administrative and cultural unity of northern and southern India. Probably this was also the main reason behind making Devgiri his capital. According to Dr. K.A. Nizami, Sultan Qutbuddin Mubarak Khalji had changed the name of Devgiri to Qutbabad and Muhammad Tughluq to Daulatabad.

s: For the first time the token currency was introduced in India by :
x: Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq launched different types of coins during his period and also decided on their reasonable prices. But the circulation of token currency was his specialty. According to Barani, due to lack of silver in treasury and policy of expanding the empire, Muhammad Tughluq had to launch the token currency. The token currency was launched in Iran during the regime of Gaykhatu, though, the experiment was unsuccessful. The token currency was successfully launched during the period of Kublai Khan. Innovative Muhammad- Bin- Tughluq was inspired by them. The modern historian also notes that there was a shortage of silver all over the world, and there was a severe shortage of silver in India too. Due to this reason, he launched token currency.

Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:

x: Barani describes the five main schemes of Muhammad Tughluq:- (1) Tax increase in Doab, (2) Devgiri (Daultabad) as Capital, (3) Issuing token currency, (4) Attack on Khurasan and (5) Qarachil expedition. The main reason behind the failure of token currency was that the state had no control over the minting of coins. The value of the token currency was equivalent to the silver value currency. As a result, many fraud mints were formed. The Lagan began to be paid by forged coins.

s: In which year did Muhammad bin Tughlaq transfer his capital to Devagiri?

s: What did the token currency introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq around 1329-30 consist of?

Silver and copper coins issued exclusively for the army

Introducing token currency in copper and brass

s: Public Works Department was primarily established by-

s: What was ‘Dar-ul-Shafa’ established by Firuz Shah Tughlaq?

s: The Sultan of Delhi who is reputed to have built the biggest network of canals in India was
x: Feroz Shah Tughlaq (r. 1351–1388) is known for constructing the largest canal network among the Delhi Sultans. The longest canal was about 200 kilometres long and ran from the river Sutlej to Hansi. Another canal was between the Yamuna and Hissar. s: The Sultan of Delhi who is reputed to have built the biggest network of canals in India was :
x: The reign of Firuz Tughluq is famous for building the biggest network of canals for irrigation purpose. They were:- (1) Sutlej river to Ghaggar (96 miles) (2) Yamuna river to Hisar (150 miles), (3) Hill of Sirmor to Hansi, (4) Ghaggar river to Firozabad and (5) Yamuna river to Firozabad. He also engraved 150 wells for irrigation and betterment of passengers. According to Firista, Firuz built 50 dams and 30 lakes at different places. Firuz Shah was the first Sultan of Delhi who imposed ‘Haqq-i-Sharb’ tax on irrigation. Those farmers who used to irrigate their fields from the water of the royal canal had to give 1/10th part of the produce to the government.

s: Which of these Sultans set up a Department of Public Works to look after building programmes?

x: The correct chronological order is Bahlol Lodi → Sikandar Lodi → Ibrahim Lodi. Bahlol Lodi founded the Lodi dynasty and ruled from about 1451 to 1489. He was succeeded by his son, Sikandar Lodi (1489–1517). After Sikandar's death, his son Ibrahim Lodi ascended the throne and ruled until 1526, when he was defeated by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat.

s: Which ruler founded the city of Agra?
x: Nizam Khan, the third son of Bahlul Lodi, ascended the throne assuming the title of Sikandar Lodi on 17 July, 1489 A.D. Sikandar Lodi was the greatest among three Lodi rulers. Sikandar Lodi is especially remembered for founding the city of Agra in 1504 A.D. with the purpose to command over eastern Rajasthan. His administration was noted for its efficiency. Roads were made safe and irrigation facilities were provided for the benefit of the peasantry. He had a knowledge of Persian poetry. He used to write poems under the nickname 'Gulrukhi'. He was known to be a kind and generous ruler who cared for his subjects.

s: Which one of the following Sultans is known for having abolished the tax on grains?
x: The rule of Lodi dynasty persisted till the coronation of Sikandar Lodi. He took keen interest in land revenue management. He ordered his nobles to present the details of their expenditure and cases of embezzlement were severely punished. He introduced “Gaj-i-Sikandari for measurement of land which was later used by Sher Shah Suri and Akbar. Several grain levies were abolished by him.

s: In 1526 Babur defeated the Sultan of Delhi, Ibrahim Lodi, at Panipat and captured _______.
x: After winning at Panipat in 1526, Babur captured Delhi and Agra along with the Lodi treasure.

s: The reason for Babur’s victory over Ibrahim Lodi was-
x: Skilled commandants were the primary reason for Babur's victory over Ibrahim Lodi.

s: The main reason for Babur’s victory in the battle of Panipat was –
x: The first battle of Panipat was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi on 21 April 1526 AD. The main reason for Babur’s victory in the battle of Panipat was his skilled warfare. The army of Babur was smaller than the army of Ibrahim Lodi, even then, he won the battle with the help of his effective warfare policy. Babur noted, “Ibrahim Lodi was an inexperienced young man careless in his movements, who marched without order, halted or retired without method and engaged without foresight.”

s: Whom did Babur defeat in the first battle of Panipat?
x: In India, artillery was used for the first time in the Battle of Panipat. But Babur mentioned the use of artillery and gun for the first time in the Battle of Bajaur (Pakistan) in 1519 A.D. The first battle of Panipat was fought on April 21, 1526 AD. It was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. The battalion of artillery was headed by Ustad Ali Quli, and the battalion of gunners was headed by Mustafa.

s: At which of the following battles was artillery used for the first time by one of the two armies?
x: In India, artillery was used for the first time in the Battle of Panipat. But Babur mentioned the use of artillery and gun for the first time in the Battle of Bajaur (Pakistan) in 1519 A.D. The first battle of Panipat was fought on April 21, 1526 AD. It was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. The battalion of artillery was headed by Ustad Ali Quli, and the battalion of gunners was headed by Mustafa.

s: The reason of Babur’s victory over Ibrahim Lodi was
x: Field artillery and muskets were the decisive factor at Panipat, with gunners Ustad Ali Quli and Mustafa, so artillery is the answer given. The notes also credit skilled warfare and commandants, which is why option 4 is tempting.

s: In which year did Babur defeat Sultan Ibrahim Lodi at the battle of Panipat?
x: Ibrahim Lodi became Sultan of Delhi in 1517 A.D. after the death of his father. He was defeated and killed by Babur on 21st April 1526 A.D. in the Battle of Panipat.

s: What was Babur's flanking manoeuvre at the First Battle of Panipat called?
x: Tulughma was the flanking manoeuvre; Araba carts chained together formed the defensive line.

s: Which military technology was described as the decisive factor in Babur’s victory at the First Battle of Panipat?
x: Babur’s field artillery and muskets were decisive factors in the victory at Panipat.

s: Why is the First Battle of Panipat considered a turning point?
o: Ended the Delhi Sultanate and began the Mughal Empire.
Ended the Vijayanagara Empire and began the Lodi dynasty.
Restored the Tughlaq state and ended Afghan rule in Bengal.
Established Rajput rule over Delhi and Agra.
x: Babur’s victory ended the Delhi Sultanate and marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire.

s: Regarding the First Battle of Panipat, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Handlers of Babur's artillery – Daulat Khan and Alam Khan
x: First Panipat was fought in 1526 against Ibrahim Lodi; artillery was decisive and was handled by Ustad Ali Quli and Mustafa.

s: What was Babur's 'Araba' at the First Battle of Panipat?
o: A flanking attack on the enemy
A cavalry charge from the rear
Carts chained together as a defence line
x: Araba was a line of chained carts, a 'Rumi' (Ottoman) device; Tulughma was the flanking attack.

s: Which of the following was one of Babur's gunners at the First Battle of Panipat?
x: Ustad Ali Quli and Mustafa were Babur's gunners.

s: Where does Babur first mention the use of guns?
x: Babur first mentions guns at Bajaur in 1519; Panipat was the first use of artillery in an Indian battle.

s: 21 April 2026 marked which anniversary of the First Battle of Panipat?
x: The battle was fought on 21 April 1526, so 2026 marked its 500th anniversary.

s: What was the approximate strength of Babur's army at the First Battle of Panipat?
x: Babur had about 12,000 men against Ibrahim's about 1,00,000.

s: Which of the following was a result of the First Battle of Panipat?
o: Babur captured Delhi, Agra and the Lodi treasure
Sher Shah founded the Sur dynasty
x: After killing Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526, Babur took Delhi, Agra and the Lodi treasure.

Which of the following battles marked the real beginning of the Mughal empire in India and set it on the path of expansion?
x: Babur won the First Battle of Panipat (1526), but the Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga consolidated Mughal power and set the empire on its path of expansion.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): The Battle of Khanua was certainly more decisive and significant than the First Battle of Panipat.
2.
Reason (R): Rana Sanga, the Rajput hero, was certainly a more formidable adversary than Ibrahim Lodi. Options:
o: Both A and R are individually true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true, but R is NOT a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: The Battle of Khanua (fought at Khanua in modern-day Rajasthan on 16 March 1527) is considered more decisive and significant than the First Battle of Panipat (April 1526) because it firmly established Mughal supremacy in North India. While Panipat gave Babur control over Delhi and Agra, the Rajput challenge under Rana Sanga still posed a serious threat to Mughal power. Rana Sanga was a far more capable and formidable opponent than Ibrahim Lodi, having united several Rajput chiefs and Afghan forces against Babur. Babur's victory at Khanua therefore crushed the strongest indigenous resistance to Mughal expansion and consolidated Mughal rule in India.

s: Who was defeated in the Battle of Khanwa?
x: Babur declared ‘Jehad’ in the battle of Khanwa. The battle of Khanwa was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga on 16 March, 1527 AD. Babur defeated Rana Sanga in this battle and assumed the title of ‘Ghazi.’

s: During which one of the following battles did Babur declare ‘Jehad’ ?
x: Babur declared ‘Jehad’ in the battle of Khanwa. The battle of Khanwa was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga on 16 March, 1527 AD. Babur defeated Rana Sanga in this battle and assumed the title of ‘Ghazi.’

x: The battle of Khatoli was fought between Maharana Sanga and Ibrahim Lodi in 1518 A.D. Ibrahim Lodi was badly defeated by Maharana Sanga.

s: In which one of the following battles, Rana Sanga fought against Babur?
x: Babur declared ‘Jehad’ in the battle of Khanwa. The battle of Khanwa was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga on 16 March, 1527 AD. Babur defeated Rana Sanga in this battle and assumed the title of ‘Ghazi.’

s: Babur attacked India in the year
x: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at First Panipat in 1526, the year his conquest of India began, so 1526 is the answer. 1527 is the year of Khanwa.

s: In which year was the Battle of Khanwa fought?
x: First Panipat was 1526, Khanwa 1527, Chanderi 1528 and Ghaghra 1529.

s: In which battle did Babur defeat Medini Rai in 1528?
x: Medini Rai was defeated at Chanderi (1528); Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527) and the Afghans at Ghaghra (1529).

s: After which battle did Babur take the title 'Ghazi'?
x: Babur declared Jehad and took the title Ghazi at Khanwa (1527), not Panipat.

s: Whom did Babur defeat in the Battle of Ghaghra (1529)?
x: At Ghaghra in 1529 Babur defeated the Afghans.

s: Why is the Battle of Khanwa regarded as more decisive than the First Battle of Panipat?
o: Artillery was used in India for the first time in it
Ibrahim Lodi was killed in it
Rana Sanga was a stronger enemy and its result set up Mughal supremacy in North India
x: At Khanwa (1527) Babur broke Rajput power under Rana Sanga, a stronger foe than Ibrahim Lodi, and set Mughal rule on firm ground.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
